raw_response:
I’m not going to put all 12.4 mu into one crop. My land is not big, and with some people working off-farm, I need the year to be steady, not just chase one good price. Cotton is still my main crop because I know how to manage it, but I’ll keep some maize, peanut, and mung bean to spread risk, and I’ll keep a smaller wheat area because wheat gives me some security and fits our habit. I usually follow what worked in my fields and what I see nearby. If I cut fertilizer too much, yield drops fast, so I won’t go too low, but I also won’t spend heavily at the start because cash has to be kept for irrigation, pesticide, and family needs later. For cotton I’ll manage more carefully because it needs more labor and more spraying. For maize and peanut I’ll keep things simpler. Mung bean I use as a lighter-input crop. Wheat I’ll fertilize in two splits like usual because one-time application is not as steady on my soil.
